prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Produce a high-fidelity desktop APPLICATION INTERFACE design mockup for a new "Prepare a delivery" feature inside Drag Shelf. This is proposed software, not a marketing poster or photograph. Output a crisp flat front-facing screenshot-like UI, landscape approximately 1440x1000, no perspective or physical monitor mockup, with readable professionally typeset text. Reference image 1 is the actual current Drag Shelf interface and is the visual identity authority: inherit warm charcoal #242520, secondary #2c2d27, cream #f4f5ee text, muted olive secondary text, yellow #f5c63a primary actions, softly rounded containers and simple consistent stroke icons. Reference 2 is the app icon; use it small in the app header. Keep original visual identity; expand the usable desktop workspace. No gradients, neon, glass decoration, fake charts, ratings, customer claims or AI branding. The user's job is prepare files for a client, understand the checks and proposed output, and preserve originals. Use one labeled "Sample project" named "Brand handoff". Show source filenames such as Brand-guide.pdf, Logo-final.png, Logo-final-copy.png, and Source-files.zip. A "Client delivery" recipe checks Final assets, Source files, Invoice and Instructions. Invoice is missing; mark it "Not added" and provide an action, do not imply all checks passed. Duplicate image copies are detected. Preparation supports consistent filenames, resize images to 1920 px, a README, and export to a new folder or ZIP. Clearly say "Originals stay unchanged". Show a practical output preview with a folder tree and original → output filename examples. Distinguish optional checks from blocking missing-file errors. Clear primary button "Review preparation", secondary "Save recipe"; compact language selector "English". Mockup text is English; ensure space for a Khmer variant during implementation. Precisely align controls, generous but purposeful spacing, usable target sizes, no repeated nested cards. All visible content must look like functional application controls and realistic sample data. Include the option label small in the image header, not as a poster heading. Option B — Guided delivery. Composition: one app window with small logo/header. A narrow LEFT vertical workflow rail occupies about 190px with four labeled steps: "1 Collect", "2 Check", "3 Prepare", "4 Export"; Check is highlighted and Collect is completed. The main pane is a focused large readiness review, with heading "Check your delivery", sample project title, and a clear summary "3 of 4 requirements covered". Display the four required delivery categories as spacious checklist rows, the Invoice row showing "Not added" with an "Add invoice" button and a quiet "Make optional" link. Below, show a duplicate issue with both filenames and "Keep one copy in output". A quiet right summary column around 260px shows the intended delivery folder, file count, recipe name and upcoming preparation settings; keep it secondary. Bottom has Back left and yellow "Continue to preparation" right, plus "Originals stay unchanged". The focus is one decision at a time, less visually dense than a full workbench. Show no dashboard metrics or card grid.
